And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter:
¶ And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
A fisherman, casting a net with his brother Andrew (Matt 4:18). James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were his “partners” (Luke 5:10).

Scripture says Philip “was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). In Capernaum Simon and Andrew had a house (Mark 1:21, 29), which Matthew calls “Peter’s house” (Matt 8:14).

CHAPTER III · THE CHURCH IN ACTS
¶ But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judæa, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:
At Pentecost he speaks for the Eleven (“Peter, standing up with the eleven”), and about three thousand are baptized (Acts 2:14–41).
The lame man at the temple gate
Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.
With John he heals a lame man at the temple gate and speaks in Solomon’s porch (Acts 3:1–26).
And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:
After a vision at Joppa he goes to the Roman centurion Cornelius at Caesarea, and the Holy Ghost falls on Gentiles (Acts 10:1–48). He defends this in Jerusalem (Acts 11:1–18).

And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
Herod kills James and then imprisons Peter; an angel leads him out. He goes to the house of Mary the mother of John Mark, then “departed, and went into another place” (Acts 12:3–17).
Herod (Agrippa I), John Mark, James, the Lord’s brother

What Scripture says of his end
Jesus tells Peter that when he is old “another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not”. John adds: “This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God” (John 21:18–19).

The writer of 2 Peter, who names himself “Simon Peter” (2 Pet 1:1), says “shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me” (2 Pet 1:14). Who wrote 2 Peter is discussed on the Letters pages.
Acts last names him at the council in Jerusalem (Acts 15:7) and never says how, where or when he died.

VIEWS, WITH WHO HOLDS THEM · THIS PAGE
When did Peter come to Rome, and how long was he there?
He and Paul founded the Roman church together

Irenaeus speaks of the church “founded and organized at Rome by the two most glorious apostles, Peter and Paul”, who then “committed into the hands of Linus the office of the episcopate”. Neither writer says how long Peter stayed.
He came to Rome at the end of his life
Origen (first half of the 3rd century), as reported by Eusebius
After preaching in Asia Minor, Peter “at last, having come to Rome, he was crucified”.
He came under Claudius and led the church for twenty-five years
Eusebius (about 325) for the arrival under Claudius; Jerome (392) for the twenty-five years
Eusebius has Peter led to Rome “during the reign of Claudius”; Jerome dates it to “the second year of Claudius” and counts twenty-five years to Nero’s fourteenth year.
